default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-1468.title: Running point-of-control cross follow
E-1468.hypothesis: The price bin with most session volume is where most participants hold positions; a close through it shifts them in or out of the money, so follow the side the price moves to.

E-1469.title: Volume-clock momentum follow
E-1469.hypothesis: Measuring the move over a fixed amount of traded volume instead of fixed time finds bursts where informed flow pushes price; follow a volume-time move that is large for its volume.

E-1470.title: Rolling-median cross with slope follow
E-1470.hypothesis: A rolling median ignores single spikes; a close crossing a median that already slopes the same way is a trend change not caused by one outlier bar.

E-1471.title: VWAP deviation peak turn fade
E-1471.hypothesis: Institutional VWAP benchmarks pull price back; when the stretch from VWAP in ATR units has peaked within the window and the bar turns, trade back toward VWAP.

E-1472.title: Prior-range outer-zone entry follow
E-1472.hypothesis: Yesterday's range split in zones: moving from the middle into the upper or lower zone means accepting prices near the old extremes; follow the move.

E-1473.title: Session-range quartile entry follow
E-1473.hypothesis: Once the session range is established, a close that enters the top or bottom quartile from inside shows the market pushing toward the extreme where stops rest; follow it.

E-1474.title: Hikkake false break reversal
E-1474.hypothesis: A break of an inside bar that fails and closes back past the opposite side traps breakout traders; their stops fuel the move the other way.

E-1475.title: Prior-session POC cross follow
E-1475.hypothesis: Yesterday's most-traded price is a reference level watched by next-day participants; a close through it signals acceptance away from yesterday's value.

E-1476.title: Early-extreme side flip
E-1476.hypothesis: When one session extreme was set early and the other was not, the morning's side lost control; a later close crossing VWAP toward the open-side confirms the day's drift.

E-1477.title: POC touch bounce
E-1477.hypothesis: A bar that dips to the session's most-traded price and closes back on its original side shows volume-defended value; trade the bounce.
